title: Senator Tracy Pennycuick shares voting reminders and veterans' resources ahead of Pennsylvania's Election Day
text:
Senator Tracy Pennycuick used her social media platform in May 2026 to provide Pennsylvania residents with reminders and resources related to Election Day and veterans’ services.
On May 18, Pennycuick posted a reminder about the upcoming election: “#ReadytoVotePA? Election Day is tomorrow, Tuesday, May 19! Polls across Pennsylvania will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.
Make sure you’re prepared before heading out to vote:
 Check your voter registration status: https://t.co/KHwoqOYV0M https://t.co/OhaYLwWo7t” (May 18, 2026).
She followed up with another post providing logistical information for voters: ” Find your polling place: https://t.co/BmZgNOJvpg
 Returning a completed mail ballot? Locate a drop box or county office: https://t.co/SzHUdbaZEr” (May 18, 2026).
On May 20, Pennycuick addressed veterans seeking assistance with military paperwork and benefits: “Veterans trying to track down military paperwork, make sure they’re not missing out on benefits they earned or get help with paperwork can turn to @PADMVA.
Call 800-547-2838 or fill out the contact form: https://t.co/bpJnbVH36Y https://t.co/1zwA3u1fDG” (May 20, 2026).
Pennycuick has a background in public service through her military career and involvement on veteran boards, contributing support for veterans and law enforcement (official website). She served for 26 years in the U.S. Army—retiring as a lieutenant colonel after participating in Desert Shield/Desert Storm—and began her career as a combat medic before earning her degree from the University of Missouri-Columbia (official website). After serving in the General Assembly, she was elected to the Pennsylvania Senate in 2022 (official website). Pennycuick resides in Harleysville with her husband, also an Army veteran, their four grown children, and two grandchildren (official website).
